what_happened: The task description rules that the bottom PR of a stack targets the integration branch. With isolation off, each task's phase commits are already on that branch, so a review branch cut from the batch's cut point cannot be merged into it in general: in a three-task fixture, merging the first review branch into the integration branch conflicted on a file a later task had also edited, and only the full-stack tip merged cleanly, as a no-op. The landing record says the review ref is 'the thing merged' without naming what it merges into. Raised as a non-blocking user decision with a measured recommendation rather than filled by guessing.

milestone-review-handoff.sh prints '/please push <integration branch>' then '/merge'. /merge acts on the checked-out branch, refuses outright on main or master, hardcodes the remote name origin and the target main, and its prompt-time grant is minted for the checked-out branch only. In a repository whose integration branch is its default branch, the printed /merge refuses; on a feature integration branch it opens one PR of the whole branch, not a stack. A review branch that is never checked out cannot be submitted through /merge as it stands.

The landing task's interface to review submission was present and unambiguous on all three owed items (ref read, per-task proof instead of a range, not one commit per task), and its blob-overlay recipe reproduced in a fresh fixture on the first attempt: three stacked review branches, one commit each, with HEAD, the index and the working tree byte-identical before and after. The same fixture showed that git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base restacks a child after its parent is squash-merged with a tree equal to a full rebuild, and unlike the overlay it keeps a foreign mainline edit to the same file.

Plan authoring: suite_selection_select returns only the full-sweep sentinel for a script and suite a plan will create, since neither exists at authoring time, so a non-final phase editing only those two files cannot name a measured suite list in its Tier Justification; the plan carries the re-measurement as a Scope Hypothesis instead.

Plan authoring: the relayed review-base decision removed the only open design question; all three flagged description premises re-validated against live state (source_dir resolves in this repository, pr-prohibition rule and guard-git-push.sh present, landing contract section present in the decision record).

review-stack-prepare.sh's refusal path initially called 'exit CODE' from inside resolver functions whose output was captured via $(...) command substitution; exit inside a command-substitution subshell only terminates that subshell, so the refusal's exit code never reached the script's own exit status (silently exit 0). Fixed by refactoring every resolver to set a global variable and calling exit as a plain statement, never inside $(...).

Prior art (milestone-review-handoff.sh's resolve_integration_branch, batch-admission-lib.sh's declared-key reader pattern, test-milestone-review-handoff.sh's deployed-shape sandbox fixture convention and static-assertion grep idiom) transplanted directly into review-stack-prepare.sh and its suite, letting Phase 1 (script + 19-case suite + registration) complete in one pass with no rework beyond the exit-code bug.

Phase 1's Batch Gate Deferral scoped check (bash .claude/scripts/verify-touched.sh, no args) ran 139+98=237 suites and reported 3 failures, none involving review-stack-prepare.sh or test-review-stack-prepare.sh: 2 were pre-existing/expected baseline failures (test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh, test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh) and 1 'NEW' (test-lint-unit-integration-boundary.sh) flagged three OTHER sibling tasks' in-flight test files (test-lean-challenge-observe.sh, test-sapience-remember.sh, test-sapience-tag-pending.sh) missing suite-classification.data rows -- unrelated to this phase's own two correctly-registered files. Phase 1 verification is clean.

685 was deferred by the in-batch admission gate on four consecutive cycles - first against 486 and then against 675 - on the __WHOLE_TREE__ sentinel and on a single shared file (git-workflow-narrative.md). Its actual implement work did not begin until cycle 5 of a 6-cycle run. The deferral reasons were correct as ordering constraints, but the batch never achieved any parallelism, so three separate /orchestrate invocations would have completed in the same wall time with less coordination overhead.

685 was admitted to orchestration as a single 7-phase task. The first implement dispatch ran 30 minutes and 127 tool calls to close Phase 1 alone, returning status=partial with 1/7 phases complete; a second continuation dispatch was required and the remaining five phases are each substantial git-plumbing and fixture work. Nothing in admission flags a plan whose phase count exceeds what one dispatch can plausibly close, so the under-decomposition was discovered only after the run was underway. The task should have been split into separate tasks before orchestration.

Cut's Phase 2 selection requirement (--milestone/--batch/--tasks) initially validated before review_base/remote/platform resolution, breaking 5 of Phase 1's success-path assertions that call 'cut --dry-run' with no selection to exercise those shared resolvers. Fixed by splitting a non-refusing rsp_gather_selection (runs first) from rsp_validate_selection (refuses 40/41/42, runs inside cut's own body after the earlier resolvers), and repointing those 5 assertions at 'show' instead of 'cut' since show's body is still the Phase 1 placeholder.

Empirically confirmed the order_contradiction refusal (exit 45) is load-bearing: disabled rsp_check_order_contradictions, re-ran the suite, observed the specific case fail with exit 0 instead of 45, then restored and observed it pass again. 28/28 passing; verify-touched.sh scoped to the two touched paths reports 98/98 passing (OWED-NOT-PAID fallback battery, same shape Phase 1 observed).

Two consecutive attempts at dispatch_seq 28 died without writing their wrap-up artifacts. The first ended when its Claude Code session exited while it was mid-Phase-3, leaving 384 uncommitted lines. Resuming that stopped agent via SendMessage then failed immediately with HTTP 400 'This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.' (request id req_011ChLYjNUkJg92sAuoRpTWE, model claude-sonnet-5) -- the saved transcript ended on an assistant turn, so the resume path could not reconstruct a valid conversation. The resume nonetheless produced further file edits before dying, so by infra-failure-discrimination.md's rule (any subagent-authored text means transport_error=false) the cycle was correctly charged rather than exempted. Postflight detected the abandoned-wrap-up signature and committed the orphaned work as 275599cff so nothing was lost. Recording because a stopped background agent whose transcript ends on an assistant turn appears to be unresumable by SendMessage, which makes the documented resume remedy unavailable for exactly the dispatches most likely to need it.

Two prior dispatch_seq-28 attempts died mid-flight without writing wrap-up artifacts, but their code work (committed as 275599cff) was already complete and correct: Phase 3's cut/show/record-request machinery (rsp_cut_plan, rsp_cut_print, rsp_overlay_tree, rsp_move_commit_onto_new_parent, manifest handling, exit codes 40-52) plus the test suite and runtime-files doc entry all existed. This re-prompt's job reduced to re-running verification in the foreground and writing the closure artifacts the prior attempts never reached.

verify-touched.sh's scoped Phase 3 battery (74 suites, OWED fallback) showed test-orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh case 3 failing once under the full parallel run inside this heavily concurrent multi-task /orchestrate batch. Re-ran the suite standalone 3 times (7/7 passing each time); concluded mtime-window timing flake under load, unrelated to review-stack-prepare.sh and not a regression. No fix applied; recorded for visibility only.
